This kernel is ONLY called when `training=True` (see line 172-183 in the CUDA host code: `if (!training) {...} else { compute_mean_var_kernel<<<...>>>(...); }`). The kernel launch is `<<<num_features, 256>>>` which is 1D, making `blockDim.x=256` and `blockDim.y=1`. With the mutation, `tid=threadIdx.y=0` for ALL 256 threads. This causes: (1) all threads process only indices 0,256,512... (1/256th of data), (2) race conditions writing to shared_sum[0], (3) reduction reads uninitialized shared_sum[1..255]. The mutant survives because testing evidence shows 'Training Mode (.train()): SKIPPED: operator_not_applicable' - the mutated code path was never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation affects only the `compute_mean_var_kernel` which is exclusively used in training mode. The test framework explicitly skipped training mode testing, marking it as 'operator_not_applicable'. In eval mode, the code branches to `batchnorm2d_forward_inference_kernel` which uses running statistics and bypasses the mutated kernel entirely. This is why 112 rounds of bitwise comparison showed identical results - the mutated code was never executed. The EMD Layer 3 analysis incorrectly concluded equivalence without recognizing that the training code path produces catastrophically wrong results (summing only 1/256th of elements).
rounds.kill_strategy: Run the model in training mode (.train()) before forward pass. With blockDim.y=1, all threads get tid=0, causing them to only process every 256th element (indices 0, 256, 512...) instead of all elements. The computed batch mean and variance will be based on only ~0.4% of the data, producing dramatically wrong normalization output. Any non-constant input distribution will expose this.
rounds.recommendations: Always exercise BOTH training and inference code paths when testing BatchNorm-like operators. The 'operator_not_applicable' skip logic incorrectly excluded a critical code path where the mutation has catastrophic effects. Test frameworks should detect which code paths contain mutations and ensure those paths are exercised regardless of default heuristics.

def generate_inputs(device):
    # Shape: [16, 64, 256, 256]
    # Create pattern where every 256th element (spatially) differs from others
    # The spatial layout is H*W = 65536 elements per channel
    # With stride=256 sampling, only elements at positions 0,256,512... are read
    x = torch.zeros(16, 64, 256, 256, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    
    # Fill with large positive values
    x.fill_(100.0)
    
    # At positions that would be sampled (every 256th in flattened spatial dim),
    # put large negative values. This creates huge statistical difference.
    # In training mode mutant: mean ≈ -100, var ≈ 0
    # Correct: mean ≈ 99.6, var ≈ very small
    x_flat = x.view(16, 64, -1)  # [16, 64, 65536]
    x_flat[:, :, ::256] = -100.0  # Set every 256th to -100
    
    return [x.contiguous()]

The testing framework runs the model in eval mode by default, and generate_inputs() has no mechanism to switch the model to training mode. Since the mutated code path is never executed in eval mode, the inference-mode kernel (batchnorm2d_forward_inference_kernel) runs instead, which is unaffected by this mutation. To kill this mutant, the testing framework would need to support: (1) model.train() calls before forward pass, or (2) a separate training-mode test track that actually invokes the training code path. The 'Training Mode: SKIPPED' result confirms this capability is missing.
